findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the vendor roster spreadsheet stored via aws_s3_bucket_object.reports_seed_object) are stored with only S3 default encryption or none at all, and no customer-managed KMS key protects the data.
The ledger_exports bucket contains financial ledger data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial exports unencrypted at rest.
The model_artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so trained model artifacts and any embedded sensitive data are stored without explicit encryption.
The ops_runbooks bucket stores operational runbooks without any server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving potentially sensitive operational procedures unencrypted at rest.
The reports_archive bucket defines no logging block, so access to the vendor roster and other reports is not recorded and cannot be audited for unauthorized access.
The ledger_exports bucket has no logging block configured, so access to financial ledger exports is unauditable.
The ops_runbooks bucket has no logging block, so accesses to operational runbooks are not captured in any audit trail.
Even the audit_trail bucket itself has no logging block, so access to the central log store is not recorded, weakening the integrity of the audit chain.

The audit_trail bucket relies on the log-delivery-write ACL and defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so account-level and policy-level settings could leave this log bucket publicly accessible; public access blocks are also absent for every other bucket in this file.

The acl = "log-delivery-write" setting grants write access to the S3 log delivery group; if the ACL is not tight or the bucket is reused, third parties could write objects into the audit trail and inject forged log entries.

force_destroy = true is set on all buckets, meaning a terraform destroy will permanently delete all objects, including audit logs and financial ledger data, without any safety check that could otherwise limit the blast radius of an accidental or malicious destroy.
The seed object uploads a vendor spreadsheet into reports_archive without specifying any server-side encryption (kms_key_id or encryption), so the sensitive vendor roster is written unencrypted.
